findings.title: AWS S3 sessionToken written to logs in plaintext (3)
findings.detail: Logged in clear text — including archived snapshot(s) edgeFwLog-230126-135900, edgeFwLog-030826-133639, edgeFwLog-100826-094101. Anyone with the log bundle can use it while it is valid. Origin: General:publish_backend_api_token. Other secrets in the same messages are masked as ****.
findings.fix: Mask this field in the connector's debug logging; treat existing bundles as sensitive and avoid sharing them outside the team.

playbook.cause: The Cloud Connector writes this secret to its debug log (also in older archived snapshots). It is a logging defect, not a breach by itself — but anyone holding the bundle can use the secret while it is valid.
steps: Treat this bundle as confidential; do not attach it to public tickets.
Tokens expire on their own; rotate if the bundle was shared widely.
Report to Engineering to mask the field in the connector log.

playbook.cause: "Invalid arguments" publish errors right after first connect to messaging.platform happen during claim/first boot before topics are assigned.
steps: If it only appears once at claim time, ignore.
If it repeats after the device is claimed, escalate with the bundle (connector publishing to an unassigned topic).

findings.title: Reconnect storms (2 hour-windows with 3+ reconnects)
findings.detail: The controller reconnected to the broker repeatedly within an hour; events published in between may be delayed or replayed.

playbook.cause: Repeated connect/disconnect within an hour usually means an unstable link (Wi-Fi, PoE/power dips) or a firewall resetting long TLS sessions.
steps: Check physical link: cable, switch port errors, PoE budget.
Look for firewall session limits/IPS resets on outbound 443.
Check controller uptime around the storm (did it reboot?).

findings.title: Network monitor reported DISCONNECTED (1)
findings.detail: The connector's own network monitor lost the cloud.

playbook.cause: The connector's own network monitor saw the cloud as unreachable — site network or Internet loss.
steps: Check the controller's network link and the site Internet at these times.
Check DNS resolution of *.hanwhavision.cloud from the site.
Correlate with MQTT disconnect findings.

findings.title: Cloud sync failed: "Failed to get Sync Object Detail" (8335) (1)
findings.detail: The cloud backend returned error 8335 while the controller fetched a sync object; that object (e.g. zones) was not synced on this pass.
findings.fix: Check whether the next sync succeeded; repeated 8335 errors are a cloud-side issue to report.

samples.text: Error in response: code: 8335 [Response: {"meta":{"code":8335,"desc":"Failed to get Sync Object Detail.","userMsg":"The system failed to get Sync Object details. Please try again."}}]

playbook.cause: Cloud backend error 8335 while fetching a sync object.
steps: Check the next sync succeeded; repeated 8335 → escalate (cloud-side).
Check whether the next sync succeeded; repeated 8335 errors are a cloud-side issue to report.
